findings.summary: AMosaic is a discontinued 1993 AmigaOS web browser port of Mosaic, notable as the first graphical browser for the Amiga platform. It introduced user-customizable interfaces via the Magic User Interface system, supported extensible image decoding through AmigaOS Datatypes, and featured an ARexx scripting interface for inter-application communication. The browser relied on Amiga networking stacks such as DNet, AmiTCP, or AS225 for connectivity.

mechanisms.title: User-customizable interface via Magic User Interface
mechanisms.explanation: The MUI system enabled full user customization of fonts, colors, and background patterns, going beyond standard Mosaic capabilities at the time.

mechanisms.title: Extensible image decoding via AmigaOS Datatypes
mechanisms.explanation: AMosaic used AmigaOS Datatypes for external and inline image decoding, allowing users to add support for new image formats by installing operating system plugins.

unknowns: Exact implementation details of the ARexx inter-application communication interface beyond documented scripting capabilities
Whether the browser included support for inline image formats beyond those covered by available Datatypes plugins
Specific networking stack configuration requirements for stable page rendering across different AmigaOS versions
